claim: Set 2025 as the baseline year for Scope 1 to 3 absolute emission reduction targets under SBTi Corporate Net Zero Standards by 2035
evidence: TSMC says it set 2025 as the baseline year for achieving Scope 1 to 3 absolute emission reduction targets under the SBTi Corporate Net Zero Standards by 2035.
notes: Strong because it includes Scope 1-3 and SBTi framing, but needs follow-up: exact percentage reduction target is not in this snippet.

claim: Overseas sites used 100% renewable energy, accounting for 14.1% of TSMC power consumption
evidence: TSMC reports overseas sites used 100% renewable energy, accounting for 14.1% of TSMC's power consumption, exceeding its 13% target.
notes: Specific, measurable, and compared against a target. Risk is lower, but Taiwan fabs remain the bigger energy challenge.

claim: Launch GREEN Agreement and supplier carbon reduction programs with major emission contributors
current_value: 230000 tons verified annual reductions; NT$84 million funding; 450000 tons projected annual CO2 reduction
evidence: TSMC reports 230,000 tons of annual supplier carbon reduction to date, NT$84 million allocated for supply chain carbon reduction projects, and a projected 450,000 tons of annual CO2 reduction.
notes: Good quantitative disclosure, but projected reductions need future verification. Important for Scope 3 credibility.

claim: Supplier environmental data and carbon transparency programs expanded through CDP and supplier data platform
current_value: 135 suppliers via CDP; 477 supplier factory datasets compiled
evidence: TSMC says 135 suppliers disclosed carbon management progress through CDP and 477 supplier factory datasets were compiled via its Supplier Environmental Information Digital Platform.
notes: Specific supplier disclosure numbers are strong. Need check whether suppliers are major enough to cover most procurement emissions.

claim: Adopted Double Materiality under ESRS and established IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards implementation plan
evidence: TSMC says it adopted the Double Materiality principle set out by ESRS and established an implementation plan for IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards to reinforce ESG governance and internal controls.
notes: Governance claim is credible and aligned with regulation, but implementation quality depends on future disclosures and assurance.

claim: SBTi-validated near-term 2030 and long-term 2050 greenhouse gas reduction targets
evidence: "ASEH says both its near-term 2030 and long-term 2050 reduction targets have been officially validated by SBTi."
notes: Strong because SBTi validation adds credibility. Need verify exact target boundary and whether Scope 3 coverage is sufficient.

claim: 19% of manufacturing facilities' energy consumption is sourced from renewables; 88% of facilities use renewable energy; 10 sites achieved RE100 certification
current_value: 19% energy consumption from renewables; 88% facilities using renewable energy; 10 RE100 sites
evidence: ASEH reports 19% of manufacturing facilities' energy consumption came from renewables, 88% of facilities used renewable energy, and 10 sites achieved RE100 certification.
notes: Specific and measurable, but 19% energy consumption from renewables still leaves a large gap to full renewable transition.

claim: Introduced 10% sustainability performance metric into supplier evaluation system
evidence: ASEH says ESG performance will constitute 10% of supplier evaluation criteria alongside quality, cost, and delivery.
notes: Good procurement integration, but 10% weighting may be too small if ESG conflicts with cost or delivery.

claim: Low-Carbon Equipment Alliance with 19 key equipment suppliers targeting 20% energy reduction by 2030
evidence: ASEH says it partnered with 19 key equipment suppliers to co-develop energy-efficient machinery aimed at achieving a 20% energy reduction by 2030.
notes: Clear target and supplier count, but future-oriented; needs tracking against actual equipment energy savings.

claim: Established cross-functional task force for IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and future sustainability-related financial disclosures
evidence: ASEH says CFO and CSO were appointed to lead IFRS sustainability disclosure work, a cross-functional task force was established, and a dedicated sustainability-related financial disclosure chapter will be included from 2027.
notes: Strong governance setup, but real credibility depends on quality of 2027 disclosures and internal control effectiveness.
